media_work.focus_or_theme: Possible wrongful execution, flawed forensic evidence (hair analysis), post-execution DNA testing
media_work.summaryNotes: Post-execution DNA contradicted trial evidence regarding a key hair sample.

media_item.focus_or_theme: Possible wrongful execution due to flawed forensic hair analysis; post-execution DNA testing revealed the hair belonged to the victim, not the executed individual.
media_item.summary_notes: This episode examines the case of Claude Howard Jones, who was executed. Post-execution DNA testing, requested by the Innocence Project, revealed that a key piece of evidence – a hair found at the crime scene – belonged to the victim, casting serious doubt on Jones' guilt.
systemic_issues_raw: Denial of DNA testing reprieve requests
policy_recommendations_raw: Greater scrutiny of forensic evidence, especially hair analysis
Wider availability and use of DNA testing, even post-conviction
Re-evaluation of cases relying heavily on accomplice testimony

research_notes_other.notes_from_film_list.txt: Post-execution investigation found key physical evidence (hair) linked to victim, not Jones, raising doubts about guilt. Available via ABC.
research_notes_other.research_findings: Searches did not confirm a specific 20/20 episode with this title. However, the details match the Claude Jones case, where post-execution DNA testing requested by the Innocence Project revealed the only physical evidence linking him to the scene (a hair) actually belonged to the victim, casting serious doubt on his guilt.

featured_individuals.crime_convicted_of_raw: Murder (of liquor store owner during robbery)
featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Claude Howard Jones was convicted of murder and executed. Post-execution DNA testing revealed that a key piece of evidence (a hair) belonged to the victim, casting significant doubt on his guilt.
contributing_factors_raw: Disputed forensic evidence (single hair strand found at scene)
Denial of DNA testing reprieve request before execution
